demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India continued to remain one of the fastest-growing major economies globally in FY26, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, resilient domestic demand and sustained policy support
- India's real estate and infrastructure sectors benefited from policy continuity, regulatory reforms and improved ease of doing business
- Decline in revenue and profit during FY26 driven by persistent delays in client payments (constraining cash flows and impacting execution timelines and billings), non-availability of sites blocked for execution of railway projects, labour constraints, and increased working capital borrowings
- Company remains confident in its long-term fundamentals and expects significant improvement in execution and financial performance in upcoming quarters
- Total unexecuted order book stood at approximately Rs 1952.76 crores as of 31 March 2026, offering healthy revenue visibility for forthcoming years
- During FY26, secured new project for construction of Unity Mall (Sector-37, HSIIDC IE Karnal, Haryana) on EPC mode, valued at Rs 142.61 crores, underscoring strong market position and continued business momentum
- After close of FY26, secured two new projects together valued at Rs 1,022.95 crores, further strengthening the order book and reflecting continued success in securing prestigious infrastructure projects

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: No plant/capacity expansion; growth comes from new EPC project awards. During FY26 the company secured the Unity Mall project (Sector-37, HSIIDC IE Karnal, Haryana) valued at Rs 142.61 crores. After the close of FY26 it secured two further projects: 12 High-rise Residential Buildings at the Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex Township, IOCL, Haryana (Package-I), valued at Rs 474.25 crores, and the Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra, Haryana, valued at Rs 548.70 crores. It also completed the redevelopment/construction of Jalandhar Cantt. Railway Station, inaugurated on 17 July 2026 under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Persistent delays in client payments constrained cash flows, impacted execution timelines, and reduced billings during FY26
- Non-availability of sites blocked for the execution of railway projects pressured operations
- Company identifies shortage of labour as a major risk area in construction projects
- The company faced pressure from increased working capital borrowings during FY26
- Flagged as inherent construction-project risks that can cause delays and cost/schedule impact
- Procurement of materials and unexpected increases in material costs identified as risk areas
- Company identifies interest rate & credit risk among the major risk areas affecting construction projects
- Safety hazards leading to accidents and injuries flagged as a major identified risk area in construction projects

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue growing through structured initiatives, improved planning, enhanced coordination, and adoption of advanced construction technologies and equipment to reduce dependence on manual labour and improve productivity
- Vision to contribute to infrastructure development across the country by executing construction projects with integrity, excellence, innovation and continuous technological advancement; aims to become an industry leader in innovative engineering and sustainable infrastructure development
- Foremost priority is to complete all projects within stipulated timelines while maintaining highest standards of quality and safety
- Internally focused on enhancing operational efficiency through robust process integration and stringent cost controls
